title: READ ... AT END / NOT AT END — twin branches; default is fall-through to next statement
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. LOAD-RECORDS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD  INPUT-FILE.
       01  INPUT-REC PIC X(80).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-EOF-FLAG PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88 IS-EOF VALUE 'Y'.
      *> AT END fires on EOF; NOT AT END fires on a successful read.
      *> Omitting NOT AT END just falls through. The two branches
      *> are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE for one READ.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       READ-NEXT.
           READ INPUT-FILE
              AT END SET IS-EOF TO TRUE
              NOT AT END PERFORM PROCESS-RECORD
           END-READ.
notes: AT END / NOT AT END is the COBOL counterpart of Fortran's END=. A Java Iterator.hasNext() is the natural rewrite; the spec must capture both branches so both translate.
